questions: What did you study in history lessons when you were at school?
Did you enjoy studying history at school? [Why/Why not?]
How often do you watch TV programmes about history now? [Why/Why not?]
What period in history would you like to learn more about? [Why?]

parts.instructions: Describe the neighbourhood you lived in when you were a child. You should say:
bullet_points: where in your town/city the neighbourhood was
what kind of people lived there
what it was like to live in this neighbourhood
and explain whether you would like to live in this neighbourhood in the future.

questions: What sort of things can neighbours do to help each other?
How well do people generally know their neighbours in your country?
How important do you think it is to have good neighbours?
Which facilities are most important to people living in a neighbourhood?
How does a neighbourhood change when new facilities (e.g. shops or schools) are built?
Should neighbourhood facilities be run by the government or by private businesses?
Do you like reading? [Why/Why not?]
What kind of books do you read?
Do you read more for pleasure or to get information? [Why?]
Do you prefer to read books on a device (e.g. an e-reader or tablet) or to read printed books? [Why?]

parts.instructions: Describe a big city you would like to visit. You should say:
bullet_points: which big city you would like to visit
and explain why you would like to visit this big city.

questions: What are the most interesting things to do while visiting cities on holiday?
Why can it sometimes be stressful to go on holiday in a big city?
Do you think it is better to go on holiday to a city or a rural area?
What are the advantages of living in a big city?
In your country, are many people moving from the country to the city?
How do you think cities of the future will be different from cities today?
What do you like to drink with your dinner?
Do you drink a lot of water every day? [Why/Why not?]
Do you prefer drinking tea or coffee? [Why?]
If people visit you in your home, what do you usually offer them to drink? [Why?]

parts.instructions: Describe a monument (e.g. a statue or sculpture) that you like. You should say:
bullet_points: and explain why you like this monument.

questions: What kinds of monuments do tourists in your country enjoy visiting?
Why do you think there are often statues of famous people in public squares?
Do you agree that old monuments and buildings should always be preserved?
Why is architecture such a popular university subject?
In what ways has the design of homes changed in recent years?
To what extent does the design of buildings affect people's moods?
Do you think it's better to use a paper map or a map on your phone? [Why?]
When was the last time you needed to use a map?
If you visit a new city, do you always use a map to find your way around? [Why/Why not?]
In general, do you find it easy to read maps? [Why/Why not?]

parts.instructions: Describe an occasion when you had to do something in a hurry. You should say:
bullet_points: why you had to do this in a hurry
and explain how you felt about having to do this in a hurry.

parts.topic: Arriving late and Managing study time
questions: Do you think it's OK to arrive late when meeting a friend?
What should happen to people who arrive late for work?
Can you suggest how people can make sure they don't arrive late?
Is it better to study in the morning or in the evening?
Why do some people find it difficult to manage their study time?
Do you agree that students should take regular breaks when studying?
